criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear rationale, users and need are identified with references. However, formal mission objectives, requirements and performance details are not specified, so it is strong Adequate rather than Accomplished.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.
Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt chart and task descriptions make the plan feasible and linked to launch, orbit, ground and comms work. It lacks contingency provisions and deeper justification, so it is not fully Accomplished.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.
Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue. Deadlines are indicated by red lines.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Some preliminary work is evident through research and STK tutorials, but no technical results, calculations or design interpretation are presented. This fits minor work completed.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Report is well structured, readable and consistently formatted. The Gantt figure is clear and footnotes match in-text markers, though references are informal URLs and the figure lacks a formal caption.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs harbour some of the most diverse species of life on the planet

technical_issues.issue: No formal mission objectives, requirements, or performance metrics such as resolution, revisit, latency or coverage.
No actual orbit, launch or space-segment design calculations; these are only planned tasks.
Preliminary progress is limited to reading and STK tutorials; no technical results or interpretation are shown.
Gantt chart lacks contingency, dependencies and explanation of grey cells; only one deadline line is evident.
Sources are bare URLs/footnotes rather than full citations; several links are not cited in the text.
Acronyms COEs and AOEs are undefined, and no sensor or data-relay architecture is specified.
Bathymetry and thermal-stress monitoring are proposed without instrument or data-product requirements.

overall: The report has a clear, well-referenced mission rationale and a feasible Gantt plan, but preliminary technical work is minimal: no design calculations, orbit/launch results, or formal requirements. Presentation is good; references are informal. C1/C2 adequate, C3 weak, C4 accomplished-low.

feedback.summary: You have a clear, well-referenced mission rationale and a feasible Gantt plan, but your preliminary technical work is minimal: no design calculations, orbit/launch results or formal requirements. Presentation is good; references are informal. To reach the next level, add formal objectives and requirements, contingency and dependencies in the plan, and show technical results.
next_steps: In Mission Concept & Rationale, convert your coral-reef rationale into formal mission objectives, requirements and performance metrics (e.g., resolution, revisit, latency, coverage), and specify instrument/data-product needs for bathymetry and thermal-stress monitoring.

In Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, add contingency provisions, task dependencies and an explanation of the grey Gantt cells; define COEs/AOEs and outline the sensor/data-relay architecture; replace bare URLs with full citations and cite all sources in text.
In Preliminary Progress, move beyond STK tutorials by presenting actual orbit, launch or space-segment design calculations and interpreting the results so your technical progress is visible.

criteria.C1: Your Mission Concept & Rationale clearly identifies users and need, e.g. near-real-time relay for coral-bleaching monitoring, with references. To move from Adequate to Accomplished, add formal mission objectives, requirements and performance metrics (resolution, revisit, latency, coverage), and specify instrument/data-product requirements for bathymetry and thermal-stress monitoring.
criteria.C2: Your Project Plan & Preliminary Progress gives a feasible Gantt chart and task descriptions linked to launch, orbit, ground and comms work. To reach Accomplished, add contingency provisions and task dependencies, explain the grey cells in Image 1, define COEs/AOEs, outline sensor/data-relay architecture, and replace bare URLs in Useful Links with full citations cited in text.
criteria.C3: You completed STK tutorials 1–4 and some research, which is useful groundwork. To move from Adequate to Accomplished, present actual technical results—orbit, launch or space-segment design calculations—with brief interpretation, rather than only planned tasks, so your preliminary progress is clearly on track.
criteria.C4: Your report is well structured and readable, with consistent formatting; Image 1 is clear and footnotes match in-text markers. To strengthen presentation, give Image 1 a formal caption and replace informal URL footnotes in Useful Links with full citations that all appear in the text.
